title: Refusal Confidence Calibration as an Adversarial-Robustness Signal

original_idea.body: Record first-token refusal probability for harmful prompts, then attack each and test whether lower-confidence refusals are more likely jailbroken; quantify predictive AUROC.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a zero-cost deploy-time jailbreak-vulnerability predictor with falsifiable AUROC criterion.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Logprob recording + standard prefill/obfuscation attacks; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment with clear success criterion.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-model red-team/monitoring signal, weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Refusal-token confidence as attack-success predictor appears untested.
